newsitem.title: USA: IIE head Bergsten says Japan seeking weaker yen.
newsitem.headline: IIE head Bergsten says Japan seeking weaker yen.

text.p: Fred Bergsten, director of the Institute of International Economics, said Thursday that he believed Japanese authorities were seeking a weaker yen in order to fuel an export-led expansion.

In remarks to reporters ahead of this week's annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, Bergsten -- who just returned to from a trip to Asia -- said he had heard figures running from 115 to as high as 125 yen to the dollar in his discussions with the Japanese.
"I think the Japanese have decided that what they really want to do is get a much weaker yen and restore export-led growth," he said.
Bergsten questioned indications that the Japanese economy, which has been largely stagnant for about five years, was beginning to show consistent expansion.
"I'm quite pessimistic about the Japanese economy," he said. He said Japanese authorities had largely run out of ways to stimulate growth, noting interest rates were nearly zero.
